energy_regime.note: Per the INSPIRE record's description, LHCf's detectors and electronics are optimised to operate during early LHC commissioning at luminosity below 10^30 cm^-2 s^-1.
energy_regime.value: LHC proton-proton (and light-ion) collisions, run mainly during early low-luminosity periods of each LHC run

facility_roles.quote: LHCf is an experiment dedicated to the measurement of neutral particles emitted in the very forward region of LHC collisions.

intervals.note: No distinct construction-start date was found; the interval runs from approval to the INSPIRE record's date_started (first collisions).

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: INSPIRE's date_completed field for this record is '9999' -- INSPIRE's own placeholder for 'not completed/ongoing', not a real date -- so it is not used and status remains 'active'. Public knowledge is that LHCf ran mainly in short low-luminosity periods early in each LHC run (2009-2010, 2013, 2015-2016) and does not run continuously through high-luminosity physics, but no source fetched in this session states that schedule at reviewable precision, so a single open 'active' interval is recorded instead of a richer run-by-run history.

physics_goals.quote: LHCf aims to help physicists interpret and calibrate large-scale cosmic-ray experiments that can cover thousands of kilometres
physics_goals.value: Measure neutral particles (mainly photons and neutrons) produced at very small angles in LHC collisions to calibrate the hadronic-interaction models used to interpret ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray air showers

summary.plain: LHCf uses two small detectors, 140 metres either side of CERN's ATLAS collision point, to study particles thrown almost exactly forward by LHC collisions -- data used to help interpret how cosmic rays create showers when they hit Earth's atmosphere.
summary.technical: Forward-physics/cosmic-ray-calibration experiment: two compact imaging sampling calorimeters (tungsten plates, plastic scintillator, position-sensitive sensors) at zero-degree collision angle, +-140 m from LHC interaction point 1, covering pseudo-rapidity > 8.4. Proposed and approved May 2004; operating since first collisions (23 Nov 2009), mainly during early low-luminosity periods of each LHC run.

unique_capabilities.quote: This is possible since the laboratory equivalent collision energy of LHC is 1017 eV.
unique_capabilities.value: Compact imaging calorimeters at zero-degree collision angle, sensitive to the pseudo-rapidity range greater than 8.4, giving LHCf access to particle production kinematics equivalent to a laboratory cosmic-ray energy of 10^17 eV
